retained.reason: This test reads the rendered Members list container to check section order. A missing container throws at this line and fails the public-route specification; it cannot produce a silent pass. The assertion is local to test markup and creates no production nullable-state rule.

The case builds two fixture entries, asserts exactly two rendered rows, then uses only their indices0 and1. A mismatched entry fails the test at the read. Keep this bounded test pairing; it is not production input handling.

These evaluations run on elements attached to the real Chromium document. Its defaultView supplies computed styles. A missing view throws and fails the browser case; it cannot be accepted as a valid geometry result. No product lifecycle or circular owner is involved.

The button is selected inside this.disclosure, so its details ancestor is the tested surface. If markup removes that ancestor, the browser evaluation fails immediately. This is a test-local DOM assumption, not a production fallback.

The loaded Members fixture has the page heading whose doubled font is asserted as64px. If the heading is missing, evaluation fails immediately. Keep the local observable check; no runtime null state or authority is hidden.
The comment states the real HTTP composition and controlled WorkOS seam, preventing application-side results from being presented as live provider evidence.
The comment connects the fixture external ID to the operator runbook constraint.
The fixture summary explains the two organizations, mixed roles/statuses and the six active product members.
The comment explains why refused pages read the session form token through the session endpoint rather than a missing page form.
The comment defines observed administration writes and excludes sign-in/refresh traffic from that evidence.
The comment distinguishes organization-wide member reads from access-resolution reads for the signed-in user.
Keep the complete-read invariant explicit: both member and invitation reads must succeed before rendering, so a partial read cannot look like a correct count or page.
The comment distinguishes null, which omits Origin, from undefined, which uses the public origin. This matters to unsafe-request specifications.
The comment defines cookie handling, the no-auto-redirect behavior and the listening/in-process transport seam. These limits explain what this protocol driver proves.
The raw string-body path deliberately preserves duplicate form fields so boundary tests can send malformed input; normal URLSearchParams conversion would lose that case.
The comment records the loopback transport and public Host/raw-header behavior that origin and routing assertions depend on.

The form reader takes hidden fields, checked radios and accessible button names while callers fill visible fields. This is the contract used by the new short-label invitation markup and its consumers.
The comment limits missing-form diagnostics to button names because hidden fields contain the session form token. Keep that disclosure constraint explicit.
Keep this protocol-reader scope note: it reads displayed pending email/role facts, not provider state or action authority.
The comment defines safe page-failure diagnostics: operator path/failure reports are allowed; credentials are not.
The credential sentinel returns only a boolean. Keep the no-secret-output limit visible beside the test guard.
The shared administrator session survives between cases. This lifetime explains the complete-group requirement and must stay explicit.
The helper uses the current visible page form and its button name before posting. Keep the public interaction boundary clear for the live cases.
Invitation tokens and links are test-only credentials. The comment identifies that sensitive scope and prevents treating their reads as safe public output.

Keep the existing live administration journey with its shared session, provider observations and credential sentinels together. UI04 updates form observations; it does not add provider operations. Splitting only to meet a line count would obscure that sequence.

The71-case inventory states the combined user journey across viewports, JavaScript states, keyboard actions and safety outcomes. Existing drivers hold mechanics. The test file has no MI goal; keep the complete behavior inventory.

This acceptance inventory uses one real HTTP composition and controlled provider seam to check related administration behavior. UI04 updates pending facts and labels without adding a product responsibility.

The integration file groups public Members rendering contracts: complete counts, native disclosure state/order, protected forms and escaping. The new cases state observable behavior; a size-only split would not create a clearer owner.
